items.title: Nvidia Fallout Looms Over Trump-Xi Meeting
items.summary: So far, President Trump has indicated that he does not plan to press the Chinese leader about U.S. intelligence findings that a Chinese spy targeted Jensen Huang.

items.title: How Jensen Huang’s Secret Led to His Downfall at Nvidia
items.summary: Nvidia’s leader said his relationship with a female customer was just about business. But what he was concealing eventually led to his resignation from the company he created.

items.title: Megaspeed Says Alice Huang Left Company in August 2025
items.summary: The Singaporean company’s statement was its first to address the status of Ms. Huang, a former executive who had a relationship with Jensen Huang of Nvidia. U.S. officials say she was spying for China.

items.title: Sean Duffy Offers New Details on How One Fix Spiraled Into Nationwide Ground Stop
items.summary: When asked, the transportation secretary could not guarantee on Sunday that a similar air traffic meltdown would not occur again.

items.title: How Could a Router Lead to a Nationwide Ground Stop?
items.summary: Aviation experts and federal officials said the network outage began after a new piece of networking equipment began flooding the rest of the system with data. The underlying cause is unclear.

items.title: A Year On, Canada’s Mark Carney Returns to China a Political Star
items.summary: Canada’s leader is courting Europe, but the bigger payoff might be in Asia, where he will share summit stages with Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and President Trump.

items.title: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, Mexican Drug Lord, Dies in Prison
items.summary: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, who helped build the foundations of modern-day drug empires, was the subject of a major U.S. manhunt for his role in the murder of a D.E.A. agent.

items.title: How Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller Built a Family in ‘Paper Tiger’
items.summary: James Gray’s latest autobiographical film, set in a crime-ridden ’80s New York, centers on what one of its stars jokingly calls “a throuple.”

items.title: International Students Are Turning Away From U.S. Universities
items.summary: For a second year, Trump administration policies appear to be scaring away international students, disrupting the finances of the American colleges that depend on them.

items.title: Chris Van Hollen Says His Majority Leader Challenge to Chuck Schumer Is Gaining Support
items.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said on Sunday that he has a “wide-open” path to unseat Chuck Schumer, the long-serving Senate Democratic leader.

items.title: Flight disruptions expected to last into Monday
items.summary: Congress recently gave the Department of Transportation $12.5 billion to upgrade the aging air traffic control system. President Trump wants more.

items.title: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
items.summary: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.

items.title: Who makes Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle jeans — and under what conditions?
items.summary: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh?

items.title: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash
items.summary: Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed.

items.title: Laws limiting coal miners' exposure to toxic dust are in danger of being rolled back
items.summary: Coal miners who are exposed to silica dust are at a higher risk of black lung disease. Despite decades of advocacy, new efforts to regulate the toxic dust are under threat.

items.title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
items.summary: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.

items.title: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't
items.summary: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.

items.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
items.summary: The film Being Heumann tells the lesser-known story of the mother of the disability rights movement. A new generation of activists share how they "carry the torch" today.

items.title: Trump blasts judge for halting his Washington golf project and says he will appeal
items.summary: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.

items.title: FAA ground stop disrupts college football
items.summary: Some college football games were delayed a few hours on Saturday or postponed to Sunday. And in Oklahoma at least, there will be perks for fans to make up for the inconvenience, including cheap beers.

items.title: Memorial opens to victims of 2015 mass shooting at Charleston church
items.summary: The memorial invites visitors to reflect on the massacre within the congregation’s long history of hardship, resilience and forgiveness.

items.title: Duffy blames Congress, prior administrations for air travel halt, chaos
items.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy refused to apologize for failures that led to the nationwide ground stop, pointing to a lack of investment in air traffic modernization.

items.title: Costco recalls whipped cream over potential cleaning chemical contamination
items.summary: A batch of a Kirkland whipped cream product sold in 12 states has been withdrawn after customers reported “a chemical smell and taste."

items.title: Airlines scramble to resume flights after ground stop as cancellations continue
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration said flight schedules are expected to return to normal by late Sunday, though some airlines warned that disruptions could persist.

items.title: Game wardens once crossed property lines. A legal movement is stopping them.
items.summary: A growing property rights campaign is reshaping how states police hunting and protect animals.

items.title: A mentor said the pain never goes away, but it can fuel powerful journalism
items.summary: A cousin who was always down for a road trip. A brilliant listener and life coach. Intimate obituaries, in 150 words or less.

items.title: Tulane granted him a diploma while investigating him for rape
items.summary: An accused student’s path through three universities highlights what experts say are gaps in college disciplinary systems.

items.title: Catholic beatification ceremony celebrates 16th-century ‘Georgia Martyrs’
items.summary: Thousands attended the beatification ceremony, which was the sixth in the United States and the first in the American South.

items.title: FAA was warned for years about repair risks leading to nationwide ground stop
items.summary: Officials said installation of a new router was behind the cancellation of more than 12,000 flights.

items.title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick’s Day event, citing DeSantis’s anti-DEI law
items.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis called it a ‘stunt,’ insisting Delray Beach is misinterpreting the Florida law.
